articleBody:
Before signing off on kitchen finish carpentry or releasing final payment, walk the room with your installer and review this practical punch-list:

- [ ] Base cabinet tops are completely level across all runs — Countertop templating requires flat surfaces to prevent gaps and broken stone.
- [ ] Wall cabinets are securely fastened into framing studs — Heavy dishware requires structural anchoring rather than drywall anchors.
- [ ] Fillers and end panels are scribed tight against the walls — Gaps along uneven drywall look sloppy and collect dirt.
- [ ] Crown molding and light rail joints meet tightly at all corners — Miters should be tight, aligned, and properly pinned.
- [ ] Cabinet doors and drawer fronts show consistent reveal gaps — Hinges and glides need final adjustment so faces sit evenly.
- [ ] Hardware pulls and knobs are installed level and uniform — Inconsistent drill locations are immediately visible once pulls are mounted.
- [ ] Toe kicks are secured flush without loose edges — Base trim must withstand daily foot contact without shifting.
- [ ] Trim joints are caulked and nail holes are filled neatly — Finish details should be ready for painter touch-ups.

How to use this checklist
Take natural light and a handheld level to inspect each run systematically. Mark any misalignments with painter's tape so your installer can make minor hinge tweaks or caulk touch-ups in one visit.
